Sign in with Apple engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Sign in with Apple workflow covers storefront language. Developer portal, Xcode, and Connect actually separate login behavior from product-page copy:

  • Sign in with Apple capability — toggled in Xcode and linked to your App ID. Controls whether the app can present Apple's login sheet. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Services ID & redirect URLs — configured in Apple Developer for web or cross-platform flows. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains private sign-in to buyers.
  • Hide My Email relay — Apple's private relay for sign-in email addresses. Your listing may mention it; configuring relay domains is engineering and portal work, not listing copy.
  • Privacy nutrition labels — App Store Connect privacy questionnaire. Filing accurate data-collection answers is compliance work — AppLocale does not complete it for you.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Sign in with Apple flags.

A working Sign in with Apple integration and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

What China buyers see when zh-Hans Sign in with Apple copy is missing

Privacy-conscious purchasers browsing the China App Store evaluate login trust in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

  • English title and subtitle — app name and tagline still Latin script while competitors show native Chinese privacy positioning
  • Untranslated login badges on screenshots — overlay lines like "Sign in with Apple", "Continue with Apple", "Hide My Email", or "One tap Sign in with Apple" remain English on zh-Hans gallery frames
  • Privacy value in English — description opens with US login marketing ("Sign in securely with Apple") that China readers skim past or misread
  • Keyword field still en-US — buyers search 通过 Apple 登录, Apple 登录, 隐藏邮件, or 隐私登录; an English-only keyword row misses China Search intent
  • Mixed page — Chinese description pasted once but screenshot captions and subtitle still English — reads unfinished next to localized competitors
  • Formal machine translation — stiff 翻译腔 for Apple's official feature names instead of the phrasing Chinese storefront readers expect (通过 Apple 登录, 隐藏邮件地址)

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps privacy-aware buyers understand login benefits before install. It does not replace Sign in with Apple engineering, Services ID configuration, or Apple's review decisions.

Sign in with Apple–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Login-centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's sign-in features — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Sign in with Apple phrasing

US pages use "Sign in with Apple", "Continue with Apple", or "One tap Sign in with Apple." Apple's official Simplified Chinese storefront vocabulary uses 通过 Apple 登录 for the feature name. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing login capabilities your app does not support.

Hide My Email value props

Screenshot overlays and description leads reference private relay email — "Hide My Email", "Keep your email private", or relay-address blurbs. Chinese buyers expect concise 隐藏邮件地址 or 保护邮箱隐私 phrasing rather than English slogans ("Your email stays hidden").

Trust and privacy positioning

Some listings reference Face ID, no-password login, or account deletion alongside Sign in with Apple. These are factual product claims in description or screenshot copy — not substitutes for implementing login flows in code, which AppLocale does not engineer.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need login-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like Apple 登录, 隐私登录, and 一键登录 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Common mistakes on Sign in with Apple zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Sign in with Apple integration localizes automatically — capability enabled; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US login badges verbatim — Latin "Continue with Apple" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Conflating listing copy with setup instructions — description explains how to enable Sign in with Apple in Settings instead of what the buyer gets; setup instructions belong in support docs, not AppLocale scope
  • Translating the in-app button label only — login sheet may show Chinese from system UI while the App Store product page stays English
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to add Sign in with Apple capability — Xcode entitlements, Services IDs, and AuthenticationServices flows are outside listing rewrite
